question_text: Which of the following ions has the maximum magnetic moment?
solution: $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^5$) has the maximum number of unpaired electrons ($5$) among the given ions ($\text{Fe}^{2+}: 4$, $\text{Ti}^{2+}: 2$, $\text{Cr}^{2+}: 4$) and therefore exhibits the maximum spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35}\text{ BM}$).

question_text: When $\text{KMnO}_4$ acts as an oxidising agent and ultimately forms $[\text{MnO}_4]^{2-}$, $\text{MnO}_2$, $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ then the number of electrons transferred in each case respectively is:
Which is the correct order of ionic sizes? (Atomic Number: $\text{Ce} = 58$, $\text{Sn} = 50$, $\text{Yb} = 70$ and $\text{Lu} = 71$)
solution: Across the lanthanide series, size decreases steadily from $\text{Ce}$ ($58$) to $\text{Yb}$ ($70$) to $\text{Lu}$ ($71$) due to lanthanide contraction, with $\text{Sn}$ lying between $\text{Ce}$ and $\text{Yb}$, giving the order $\text{Ce} > \text{Sn} > \text{Yb} > \text{Lu}$.

question_text: Arrange $\text{Ce}^{3+}$, $\text{La}^{3+}$, $\text{Pm}^{3+}$ and $\text{Yb}^{3+}$ in increasing order of their ionic radii:
solution: Due to lanthanide contraction, the ionic radii of trivalent lanthanide ions decrease steadily with increasing atomic number ($\text{La}: 57$, $\text{Ce}: 58$, $\text{Pm}: 61$, $\text{Yb}: 70$). Hence, $\text{Yb}^{3+} < \text{Pm}^{3+} < \text{Ce}^{3+} < \text{La}^{3+}$.

question_text: Most common oxidation states of $\text{Ce}$ (cerium) are:
solution: Cerium ($[\text{Xe}]4f^1 5d^1 6s^2$) exhibits the characteristic lanthanide oxidation state of $+3$ ($[\text{Xe}]4f^1$) as well as $+4$ ($[\text{Xe}]4f^0$), which is stabilised by achieving a noble gas configuration.

question_text: The atomic numbers of vanadium ($\text{V}$), chromium ($\text{Cr}$), manganese ($\text{Mn}$) and iron ($\text{Fe}$) are respectively $23, 24, 25$ and $26$. Which one of these may be expected to have the highest second ionization enthalpy?
solution: After losing one electron, $\text{Cr}^+$ attains the extra-stable half-filled configuration $[\text{Ar}]3d^5$. Removing a second electron from this half-filled $3d^5$ subshell requires the highest energy, giving $\text{Cr}$ the highest second ionisation enthalpy.

question_text: The number of $d$-electrons retained in $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ (At. no. of $\text{Fe} = 26$) ion is:
solution: $\text{Fe}$ ($Z = 26$): $[\text{Ar}]3d^6 4s^2 \implies \text{Fe}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}]3d^6 4s^0$. Thus, $6$ $d$-electrons are retained in $\text{Fe}^{2+}$.

question_text: What would happen when a solution of potassium chromate is treated with an excess of dilute nitric acid?
solution: In acidic medium, yellow chromate ions dimerise to form orange dichromate ions and water: $2\text{CrO}_4^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightleftharpoons \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

question_text: A red solid is insoluble in water. However it becomes soluble if some $\text{KI}$ is added to water. Heating the red solid in a test tube results in liberation of some violet coloured fumes and droplets of a metal appear on the cooler parts of the test tube. The red solid is:
solution: Red $\text{HgI}_2$ dissolves in aqueous $\text{KI}$ to form soluble $\text{K}_2[\text{HgI}_4]$ (Nessler's reagent), and upon heating decomposes into metallic mercury droplets and violet $\text{I}_2$ vapours: $\text{HgI}_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Hg} + \text{I}_2$.

question_text: Which one of the following is an amphoteric oxide?
solution: $\text{ZnO}$ reacts with both acids and alkalies to form salts and water, so it is an amphoteric oxide ($\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is basic, while $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{B}_2\text{O}_3$ are acidic).

question_text: A reduction in atomic size with increase in atomic number is a characteristic of elements of:
solution: $f$-Block elements exhibit a steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii with increasing atomic number due to poor shielding by $4f$ / $5f$ electrons (lanthanide and actinide contractions).

question_text: The radius of $\text{La}^{3+}$ (Atomic number of $\text{La} = 57$) is $1.06\text{ \AA}$. Which one of the following given values will be closest to the radius of $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ (Atomic number of $\text{Lu} = 71$)?
solution: Due to lanthanide contraction across the $4f$ series, the ionic radius decreases significantly from $\text{La}^{3+}$ ($1.06\text{ \AA}$) to $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ ($0.85\text{ \AA}$).

question_text: Of the following outer electronic configurations of atoms, the highest oxidation state is achieved by which one of them?
solution: An atom with outer configuration $(n-1)d^5 ns^2$ (such as $\text{Mn}$ or $\text{Re}$) has $7$ unpaired/valence electrons available for bonding, achieving the highest oxidation state of $+7$.

question_text: Cerium ($Z = 58$) is an important member of the lanthanoids. Which of the following statements about cerium is incorrect?
options: The common oxidation states of cerium are $+3$ and $+4$
Cerium(IV) acts as an oxidizing agent
The $+4$ oxidation state of cerium is not known in solutions
The $+3$ oxidation state of cerium is more stable than the $+4$ oxidation state
solution: Cerium(IV) is well known in aqueous solutions (such as ceric ammonium nitrate) and is widely used as a volumetric oxidising agent, making statement (C) incorrect.

question_text: The oxidation state of chromium in the final product formed by the reaction between $\text{KI}$ and acidified potassium dichromate solution is:
solution: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6\text{I}^- \longrightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3\text{I}_2$. Chromium is reduced from $+6$ to $+3$.

question_text: Heating mixture of $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{Cu}_2\text{S}$ will give:
solution: Auto-reduction of copper takes place on heating $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{Cu}_2\text{S}$: $2\text{Cu}_2\text{O} + \text{Cu}_2\text{S} \xrightarrow{\Delta} 6\text{Cu} + \text{SO}_2$.

question_text: Which of the following factors may be regarded as the main cause of lanthanide contraction?
options: Poor shielding of one of $4f$ electron by another in the subshell
Poor shielding of one of $4f$ electron by another in the subshell
Poorer shielding of $5d$ electrons by $4f$ electrons
Greater shielding of $5d$ electrons by $4f$ electrons
solution: Because of the diffuse shape of $4f$ orbitals, one $4f$ electron provides very poor shielding to another $4f$ electron from the increasing nuclear charge across the lanthanide series, resulting in lanthanide contraction.

question_text: The lanthanide contraction is responsible for the fact that:
options: $\text{Zr}$ and $\text{Y}$ have about the same radius
$\text{Zr}$ and $\text{Hf}$ have about the same radius
$\text{Zr}$ and $\text{Zn}$ have the same oxidation state
solution: Due to lanthanide contraction, the post-lanthanide $5d$ transition elements have nearly identical atomic and ionic radii to the corresponding $4d$ transition elements (e.g., $\text{Zr} = 160\text{ pm}$ and $\text{Hf} = 159\text{ pm}$).

question_text: Lanthanoid contraction is caused due to:
options: the appreciable shielding on outer electrons by $4f$ electrons from the nuclear charge
the appreciable shielding on outer electrons by $5d$ electrons from the nuclear charge
the same effective nuclear charge from $\text{Ce}$ to $\text{Lu}$
the imperfect shielding on outer electrons by $4f$ electrons from the nuclear charge
solution: Lanthanoid contraction is caused by the imperfect (poor) shielding of outer valence electrons by $4f$ electrons as nuclear charge increases from $\text{Ce}$ to $\text{Lu}$.

question_text: The "spin-only" magnetic moment [in units of Bohr magneton, ($\mu_B$)] of $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ in aqueous solution would be (Atomic number of $\text{Ni} = 28$):
solution: $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($Z = 28$) has configuration $[\text{Ar}]3d^8$, which contains $n = 2$ unpaired electrons. Spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} = 2.83\text{ BM} \approx 2.84\text{ BM}$.

question_text: Identify the incorrect statement among the following:
options: $d$-Block elements show irregular and erratic chemical properties among themselves
$\text{La}$ and $\text{Lu}$ have partially filled $d$ orbitals and no other partially filled orbitals
The chemistry of various lanthanoids is very similar
solution: $5f$ orbitals are more diffuse and extend further from the nucleus than $4f$ orbitals, so $5f$ electrons are even less effectively shielded than $4f$ electrons. Thus, $4f$ and $5f$ orbitals are not equally shielded.

question_text: Which of the following nuclear reactions will generate an isotope?
solution: $^A_Z\text{X} \longrightarrow ^{A-1}_Z\text{X} + ^1_0n$. Emission of a neutron changes only the mass number ($A$) while keeping the atomic number ($Z$) unchanged, generating an isotope of the parent element.

question_text: The actinoids exhibit more number of oxidation states in general than the lanthanoids. This is because:
options: the $5f$ orbitals are more buried than the $4f$ orbitals
there is a similarity between $4f$ and $5f$ orbitals in their angular part of the wave function
the actinoids are more reactive than the lanthanoids
the $5f$ orbitals extend further from the nucleus than the $4f$ orbitals
solution: The $5f$ orbitals extend further from the nucleus than the $4f$ orbitals and have energies very close to the $6d$ and $7s$ orbitals, allowing $5f$ electrons to participate readily in bonding and exhibit a wider range of oxidation states.

question_text: Amount of oxalic acid present in a solution can be determined by its titration with $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution in the presence of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. The titration gives unsatisfactory result when carried out in the presence of $\text{HCl}$, because $\text{HCl}$:
options: gets oxidised by oxalic acid to chlorine
furnishes $\text{H}^+$ ions in addition to those from oxalic acid
oxidises oxalic acid to carbon dioxide and water
solution: $\text{HCl}$ cannot be used to acidify $\text{KMnO}_4$ titrations because $\text{Cl}^-$ reduces $\text{MnO}_4^-$ to $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ while itself getting oxidised to $\text{Cl}_2$, consuming extra $\text{KMnO}_4$.

question_text: Larger number of oxidation states are exhibited by the actinoids than those by the lanthanoids, the main reason being:
options: $4f$ orbitals more diffused than the $5f$ orbitals
lesser energy difference between $5f$ and $6d$ than between $4f$ and $5d$ orbitals
more energy difference between $5f$ and $6d$ than between $4f$ and $5d$ orbitals
more reactive nature of the actinoids than the lanthanoids
solution: The energy gap between $5f$, $6d$, and $7s$ subshells in actinoids is much smaller than that between $4f$, $5d$, and $6s$ subshells in lanthanoids, allowing electrons from all three subshells to participate in bonding.

question_text: In context with the transition elements, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In addition to the normal oxidation states, the zero oxidation state is also shown by these elements in complexes.
In the highest oxidation states, the transition metals show basic character and form cationic complexes.
In the highest oxidation states of the first five transition elements ($\text{Sc}$ to $\text{Mn}$), all the $4s$ and $3d$ electrons are used for bonding.
Once the $d^5$ configuration is exceeded, the tendency to involve all the $3d$ electrons in bonding decreases.
solution: In their highest oxidation states (such as $\text{CrO}_3$, $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$), transition metals have high positive charge density and show acidic character, forming oxoanions ($\text{CrO}_4^{2-}, \text{MnO}_4^-$) rather than basic cationic complexes.

question_text: Knowing that the chemistry of lanthanoids ($\text{Ln}$) is dominated by its $+3$ oxidation state, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Because of the large size of the $\text{Ln}(\text{III})$ ions the bonding in its compounds is predominantly ionic in character.
The ionic sizes of $\text{Ln}(\text{III})$ decrease in general with increasing atomic number.
$\text{Ln}(\text{III})$ hydroxides are mainly basic in character.
solution: Most trivalent lanthanoid ions ($\text{Ln}^{3+}$) contain partially filled $4f$ orbitals ($4f^1$ to $4f^{13}$) and are coloured in both the solid state and aqueous solution due to $f-f$ transitions (only $4f^0$, $4f^7$, and $4f^{14}$ ions are colourless).

question_text: The outer electron configuration of $\text{Gd}$ (Atomic No: $64$) is:
solution: Gadolinium ($Z = 64$) has the outer electronic configuration $4f^7 5d^1 6s^2$ because the half-filled $4f^7$ subshell provides extra exchange-energy stability.

question_text: In context of the lanthanoids, which of the following statements is not correct?
options: All the members exhibit $+3$ oxidation state.
Because of similar properties the separation of lanthanoids is not easy.
Availability of $4f$ electrons results in the formation of compounds in $+4$ state for all the members of the series.
There is a gradual decrease in the radii of the members with increasing atomic number in the series.
solution: The principal oxidation state of all lanthanoids is $+3$; only a few elements (such as $\text{Ce}, \text{Pr}, \text{Nd}, \text{Tb}, \text{Dy}$) exhibit the $+4$ oxidation state, not all members of the series.

question_text: Iron exhibits $+2$ and $+3$ oxidation states. Which of the following statements about iron is incorrect?
options: Ferrous oxide is more basic in nature than the ferric oxide.
Ferrous compounds are relatively more ionic than the corresponding ferric compounds.
Ferrous compounds are less volatile than the corresponding ferric compounds.
Ferrous compounds are more easily hydrolysed than the corresponding ferric compounds.
solution: Ferric ion ($\text{Fe}^{3+}$) has a higher charge-to-radius ratio (higher polarising power) than ferrous ion ($\text{Fe}^{2+}$), so ferric compounds are more covalent, more volatile, less basic, and more easily hydrolysed than ferrous compounds. Thus, statement (D) is incorrect.

question_text:
The $d$-electron configurations of $\text{Cr}^{2+}, \text{Mn}^{2+}, \text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{Co}^{2+}$ are $d^4, d^5, d^6$ and $d^7$ respectively. Which one of the following will exhibit the lowest paramagnetic behaviour?
(Atomic no. $\text{Cr} = 24, \text{Mn} = 25, \text{Fe} = 26, \text{Co} = 27$).
solution: With weak field $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ligands, the numbers of unpaired electrons are: $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($d^4 \to 4$), $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($d^5 \to 5$), $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($d^6 \to 4$), and $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ($d^7 \to 3$). Since $\text{Co}^{2+}$ has the fewest unpaired electrons, $[\text{Co}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ exhibits the lowest paramagnetic behaviour.

question_text:
Which is not the correct statement?
(At. nos. $\text{Ce} = 58, \text{Lu} = 71, \text{La} = 57, \text{Yb} = 70$)
solution: $\text{Yb}^{3+}$ ($[\text{Xe}]4f^{13}$) absorbs only in the infrared region and is colourless in aqueous solution, not pink.

question_text: Magnetic moment of $\text{Gd}^{3+}$ ion ($Z = 64$) is:
solution: $\text{Gd}$ ($Z = 64$): $[\text{Xe}]4f^7 5d^1 6s^2 \implies \text{Gd}^{3+}: [\text{Xe}]4f^7$. With $n = 7$ unpaired electrons, $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{7(7+2)} = \sqrt{63} = 7.93\text{ BM} \approx 7.9\text{ BM}$.

question_text: Reagent used to convert allyl alcohol to acrolein is:
solution: Active manganese dioxide ($\text{MnO}_2$) selectively oxidises allylic primary alcohols ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) to $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated aldehydes ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}$, acrolein) without over-oxidising to the carboxylic acid or cleaving the double bond.

question_text:
Which of the following paramagnetic ions would exhibit a magnetic moment (spin only) of the order of $5\text{ BM}$?
(At. Nos. $\text{Mn} = 25, \text{Cr} = 24, \text{V} = 23, \text{Ti} = 22$)
solution: $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($3d^4$) has $n = 4$ unpaired electrons, giving $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} = 4.90\text{ BM} \approx 5\text{ BM}$ ($\text{Mn}^{2+}: 5.92\text{ BM}$, $\text{V}^{2+}: 3.87\text{ BM}$, $\text{Ti}^{2+}: 2.83\text{ BM}$).

question_text: The number of unpaired electrons in Gadolinium ($Z = 64$) is:
solution: Ground-state electronic configuration of $\text{Gd}$ ($Z = 64$) is $[\text{Xe}]4f^7 5d^1 6s^2$, which has $7$ unpaired electrons in $4f$ and $1$ unpaired electron in $5d$, giving a total of $8$ unpaired electrons.

question_text: Which of the following forms stable $+4$ oxidation state?
solution: Cerium ($Z = 58$, $[\text{Xe}]4f^1 5d^1 6s^2$) readily loses all four outer electrons to form $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ with a stable noble-gas configuration ($[\text{Xe}]4f^0$).

question_text:
Given:
$E^\circ_{\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}} = -0.74\text{ V};\; E^\circ_{\text{MnO}_4^-/\text{Mn}^{2+}} = 1.51\text{ V}$
$E^\circ_{\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}/\text{Cr}^{3+}} = 1.33\text{ V};\; E^\circ_{\text{Cl}_2/\text{Cl}^-} = 1.36\text{ V}$
Based on the data given above, strongest oxidising agent will be:
solution: The species with the highest standard reduction potential ($E^\circ_{\text{MnO}_4^-/\text{Mn}^{2+}} = +1.51\text{ V}$) has the greatest tendency to gain electrons (be reduced) and is therefore the strongest oxidising agent ($\text{MnO}_4^-$).

question_text: Which of the following arrangements does not represent the correct order of the property stated against it?
solution: Number of unpaired electrons: $\text{V}^{2+}$ ($3d^3 \to 3$), $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($3d^4 \to 4$), $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($3d^5 \to 5$), $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($3d^6 \to 4$). Therefore, paramagnetic behaviour follows $\text{V}^{2+} < \text{Cr}^{2+} = \text{Fe}^{2+} < \text{Mn}^{2+}$, making option (C) incorrect.

question_text: The element with which of the following outer electron configuration may exhibit the largest number of oxidation states in its compounds:
solution: The element with outer configuration $3d^5 4s^2$ is manganese ($\text{Mn}$), which exhibits the largest number of oxidation states in the $3d$ series, ranging from $+2$ to $+7$ ($+2, +3, +4, +5, +6, +7$).

question_text: Potassium dichromate when heated with concentrated sulphuric acid and a soluble chloride, gives brown-red vapours of:
solution: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 4\text{NaCl} + 6\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{KHSO}_4 + 4\text{NaHSO}_4 + 2\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2\uparrow + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Orange-red vapours of chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) are evolved.

question_text: Identify incorrect statement:
options: Copper(I) compounds are colourless except when colour results from charge transfer.
solution: Cuprous oxide ($\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$) is red in colour (due to ligand-to-metal charge transfer), not colourless. Thus, statement (A) is incorrect.

question_text: When a small amount of $\text{KMnO}_4$ is added to concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, a green oily compound is obtained which is highly explosive in nature. Compound may be:
solution: $2\text{KMnO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(\text{conc.}) \longrightarrow \text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7 + 2\text{KHSO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Manganese heptoxide ($\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$) is a dark green oily liquid that is highly explosive.

question_text: The equation which is balanced and represents the correct product(s) is:
solution: In $[\text{CoCl}(\text{NH}_3)_5]^+ + 5\text{H}^+ \longrightarrow \text{Co}^{2+} + 5\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{Cl}^-$, both atoms and total charge ($+6$ on each side) are balanced and the products are correct. (In C, the product charge should be $2-$; in D, $\text{K}_3[\text{Cu}(\text{CN})_4]$ and $(\text{CN})_2$ are formed).

question_text: Which of the following is not formed when $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ reacts with acidic $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ solution?
solution: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 4\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + 3\text{H}_2\text{S} \longrightarrow \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{Cr}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3\text{S}$. Chromium is reduced to $+3$ ($\text{Cr}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$), so $\text{CrSO}_4$ ($+2$) is not formed.

question_text: Copper becomes green when exposed to moist air for a long period. This is due to:
options: the formation of a layer of cupric oxide on the surface of copper.
the formation of a layer of basic carbonate of copper on the surface of copper.
the formation of a layer of cupric hydroxide on the surface of the metal.
the formation of basic copper sulphate layer on the surface of copper.
solution: When exposed to moist air containing $\text{CO}_2$, copper develops a green patina due to the formation of basic copper(II) carbonate, $\text{CuCO}_3\cdot \text{Cu}(\text{OH})_2$.

question_text: Which one of the following exhibits the largest number of oxidation states?
solution: Manganese ($\text{Mn}, Z = 25, [\text{Ar}]3d^5 4s^2$) exhibits the largest number of oxidation states among the first transition series ($+2, +3, +4, +5, +6, +7$).

question_text: Which one of the following compounds is not a yellow colored compound?
solution: $\text{BaCrO}_4$, $\text{K}_3[\text{Co}(\text{NO}_2)_6]$, and $(\text{NH}_4)_3\text{As}(\text{Mo}_3\text{O}_{10})_4$ are yellow precipitates, whereas zinc ferrocyanide, $\text{Zn}_2[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$, is white/bluish-white.

question_text: The colour of $\text{KMnO}_4$ is due to [where $\text{M} \to \text{metal}$, $\text{L} \to \text{ligand}$]:
solution: In $\text{MnO}_4^-$, $\text{Mn}^{7+}$ has a $3d^0$ configuration so $d-d$ transitions are not possible. Its intense purple colour arises from ligand-to-metal ($\text{L} \to \text{M}$) charge transfer from filled $2p$ orbitals of $\text{O}^{2-}$ ligands to empty $3d$ orbitals of $\text{Mn}^{7+}$.

question_text:
Match the catalysts to the correct processes:
Catalyst: (A) $\text{TiCl}_3$, (B) $\text{PdCl}_2$, (C) $\text{CuCl}_2$, (D) $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$
Process: (i) Wacker process, (ii) Ziegler-Natta polymerisation, (iii) Contact process, (iv) Deacon's process

An aqueous solution of a salt $\text{X}$ turns blood red on treatment with $\text{SCN}^-$ and blue on treatment with $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$. $\text{X}$ also gives a positive chromyl chloride test. The salt $\text{X}$ is:
solution: $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ reacts with $\text{SCN}^-$ to form blood-red $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$ and with $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$ to give Prussian blue $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$. A positive chromyl chloride test confirms the presence of $\text{Cl}^-$. Hence, salt $\text{X}$ is $\text{FeCl}_3$.

question_text: Which of the following statements is/are false?
options: $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is the primary standard in volumetry.
solution: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is used as a primary standard in volumetric analysis rather than $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ because $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is hygroscopic and absorbs moisture from the atmosphere. Thus, statement (C) is false.

question_text: Find the metallic and ferromagnetic substance:
solution: Chromium(IV) oxide ($\text{CrO}_2$) exhibits metallic conductivity and is ferromagnetic (used in magnetic recording tapes).

question_text: Which one of the following species is stable in aqueous solution?
solution: $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$ is stable in alkaline aqueous solution, whereas $\text{Cu}^+$ disproportionates into $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cu}$, $\text{MnO}_4^{3-}$ disproportionates into $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$ and $\text{MnO}_2$, and $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ is readily oxidised to $\text{Cr}^{3+}$.

question_text: Which of the following are the transition metal ions responsible for colour in ruby and emerald respectively?
solution: In both ruby (corundum, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) and emerald (beryl, $\text{Be}_3\text{Al}_2(\text{SiO}_3)_6$), trace $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ions replacing $\text{Al}^{3+}$ in octahedral sites are responsible for the colour.

question_text: The sodium salt of an organic acid $\text{X}$ produces effervescence with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. $\text{X}$ reacts with the acidified aqueous $\text{CaCl}_2$ solution to give a white precipitate which decolourises acidic solution of $\text{KMnO}_4$. $\text{X}$ is:
solution: $\text{Na}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$ evolves $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CO}_2$ effervescence with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, forms a white precipitate of $\text{CaC}_2\text{O}_4$ with $\text{CaCl}_2$, and decolourises acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$.

question_text:
In the following reactions, $\text{ZnO}$ is respectively acting as a/an:
(i) $\text{ZnO} + \text{Na}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{ZnO}_2$
(ii) $\text{ZnO} + \text{CO}_2 \longrightarrow \text{ZnCO}_3$
solution: In reaction (i), $\text{ZnO}$ reacts with basic $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ to form sodium zincate, acting as an acid. In reaction (ii), $\text{ZnO}$ reacts with acidic $\text{CO}_2$ to form $\text{ZnCO}_3$, acting as a base.

question_text: The correct order of spin-only magnetic moments among the following is (Atomic number: $\text{Mn} = 25, \text{Co} = 27, \text{Ni} = 28, \text{Zn} = 30$):
solution: Number of unpaired electrons: $[\text{MnCl}_4]^{2-}$ ($\text{Mn}^{2+}, 3d^5 \to 5$), $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$ ($\text{Co}^{2+}, 3d^7 \to 3$), $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ ($\text{Ni}^{2+}, 3d^8 \to 2$), $[\text{ZnCl}_4]^{2-}$ ($\text{Zn}^{2+}, 3d^{10} \to 0$). Hence, $[\text{MnCl}_4]^{2-} > [\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-} > [\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-} > [\text{ZnCl}_4]^{2-}$.

question_text: The incorrect statement is:
options: $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ion gives chocolate coloured precipitate with potassium ferrocyanide solution
$\text{Cu}^{2+}$ and $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ions give black precipitate with $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ in presence of $\text{HCl}$ solution
Ferric ion gives blood red colour with potassium thiocyanate
$\text{Cu}^{2+}$ salts give red coloured borax bead test in reducing flame
solution: $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ (Group II) gives a black precipitate of $\text{CuS}$ with $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ in acidic $\text{HCl}$ medium, whereas $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ (Group IV) precipitates as $\text{NiS}$ only in alkaline medium ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$). Thus, statement (B) is incorrect.

question_text: When $\text{XO}_2$ is fused with an alkali metal hydroxide in presence of an oxidizing agent such as $\text{KNO}_3$, a dark green product is formed which disproportionates in acidic solution to afford a dark purple solution. $\text{X}$ is:
solution: $2\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{KOH} + \text{O}_2 \longrightarrow 2\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4\text{ (dark green)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$; in acidic medium, $3\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ \longrightarrow 2\text{MnO}_4^-\text{ (dark purple)} + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Hence, $\text{X}$ is $\text{Mn}$.

question_text: The transition element that has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation is:
solution: Zinc ($\text{Zn}, [\text{Ar}]3d^{10}4s^2$) has completely filled $3d$ orbitals and no unpaired $d$-electrons to form strong metallic bonds, giving it the lowest enthalpy of atomisation ($126\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) among the $3d$ elements.

question_text: The effect of lanthanoid contraction in the lanthanoid series of elements by and large means:
options: increase in atomic radii and decrease in ionic radii
decrease in atomic radii and increase in ionic radii
increase in both atomic and ionic radii
decrease in both atomic and ionic radii
solution: Across the lanthanoid series, imperfect shielding by $4f$ electrons causes an increase in effective nuclear charge, leading to a steady decrease in both atomic and ionic radii.

question_text: The element that usually does NOT show variable oxidation states is:
solution: Scandium ($\text{Sc}, [\text{Ar}]3d^1 4s^2$) loses all three valence electrons to achieve a noble-gas core ($\text{Sc}^{3+}$) and exhibits only $+3$ oxidation state in its compounds.

solution: $\text{La}^{3+}$ ($4f^0$), $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ ($4f^{14}$), and $\text{Gd}^{3+}$ ($4f^7$, stable half-filled) are colourless, whereas $\text{Sm}^{3+}$ ($4f^5$) is pale yellow due to $f-f$ electronic transitions.

question_text: The statement that is INCORRECT about the interstitial compounds is:
solution: Interstitial compounds have high melting points, are very hard, retain metallic conductivity, and are chemically inert (not chemically reactive).

question_text: The number of water molecules not coordinated to copper ion directly in $\text{CuSO}_4\cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is:
solution: In $[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4]\text{SO}_4\cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$, $4$ water molecules are directly coordinated to $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ while $1$ water molecule is hydrogen-bonded outside the coordination sphere as water of crystallisation.

question_text: The maximum number of possible oxidation states of actinoids are shown by:
solution: Neptunium ($\text{Np}$) and plutonium ($\text{Pu}$) show the maximum number of oxidation states among the actinoids, ranging from $+3$ to $+7$ ($+3, +4, +5, +6, +7$).

question_text: Consider the hydrated ions of $\text{Ti}^{2+}, \text{V}^{2+}, \text{Ti}^{3+}$ and $\text{Sc}^{3+}$. The correct order of their spin-only magnetic moments is:
solution: Number of unpaired electrons: $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ ($3d^0 \to 0$), $\text{Ti}^{3+}$ ($3d^1 \to 1$), $\text{Ti}^{2+}$ ($3d^2 \to 2$), $\text{V}^{2+}$ ($3d^3 \to 3$). Thus, the spin-only magnetic moments follow $\text{Sc}^{3+} < \text{Ti}^{3+} < \text{Ti}^{2+} < \text{V}^{2+}$.

question_text: The highest possible oxidation states of uranium and plutonium, respectively, are:
solution: Uranium ($[\text{Rn}]5f^3 6d^1 7s^2$) shows a maximum oxidation state of $+6$ (e.g., $\text{UF}_6$), while plutonium ($[\text{Rn}]5f^6 7s^2$) shows a maximum oxidation state of $+7$ (e.g., $\text{PuO}_5^{3-}$).

question_text: The metal that gives hydrogen gas upon treatment with both the acid as well as the base is:
solution: Zinc is amphoteric and liberates $\text{H}_2$ gas with both dilute acids ($\text{Zn} + 2\text{HCl} \longrightarrow \text{ZnCl}_2 + \text{H}_2$) and strong bases ($\text{Zn} + 2\text{NaOH} \longrightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{ZnO}_2 + \text{H}_2$).

question_text: Thermal decomposition of a $\text{Mn}$ compound ($\text{X}$) at $513\text{ K}$ results in compound $\text{Y}$, $\text{MnO}_2$ and a gaseous product. $\text{MnO}_2$ reacts with $\text{NaCl}$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to give a pungent gas $\text{Z}$. $\text{X}$, $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$, respectively, are:
solution:
$2\text{KMnO}_4(\text{X}) \xrightarrow{513\text{ K}} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4(\text{Y}) + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2(g)$;
$\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{NaCl} + 4\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \text{MnCl}_2 + 4\text{NaHSO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Cl}_2(g)(\text{Z})$.

question_text: The pair that has similar atomic radii is:
solution: Due to lanthanoid contraction, $\text{Mo}$ ($4d$ series, $139\text{ pm}$) and $\text{W}$ ($5d$ series, $139\text{ pm}$) have virtually identical atomic radii.

question_text: The atomic radius of $\text{Ag}$ is closest to:
solution: Due to lanthanoid contraction, the atomic radius of $\text{Ag}$ ($4d$ series, $144\text{ pm}$) is almost identical to that of $\text{Au}$ ($5d$ series, $144\text{ pm}$).

question_text: The electronic configurations of bivalent europium and trivalent cerium are (atomic number: $\text{Xe} = 54, \text{Ce} = 58, \text{Eu} = 63$):
solution:
$\text{Eu}$ ($Z = 63$): $[\text{Xe}]4f^7 6s^2 \implies \text{Eu}^{2+}: [\text{Xe}]4f^7$.
$\text{Ce}$ ($Z = 58$): $[\text{Xe}]4f^1 5d^1 6s^2 \implies \text{Ce}^{3+}: [\text{Xe}]4f^1$.

question_text: The sum of the total number of bonds between chromium and oxygen atoms in chromate and dichromate ions is ______.
solution: In chromate ion ($\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$), there are $4$ $\text{Cr}-\text{O}$ linkages ($2\;\text{Cr}=\text{O} + 2\;\text{Cr}-\text{O}^-$). In dichromate ion ($\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$), each $\text{Cr}$ is bonded to $4$ oxygen atoms, giving $8$ $\text{Cr}-\text{O}$ linkages ($4\;\text{Cr}=\text{O} + 2\;\text{Cr}-\text{O}^- + 2\;\text{Cr}-\text{O}$ bridging). Total $= 4 + 8 = 12$.

question_text: The oxidation states of transition metal atoms in $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$, $\text{KMnO}_4$ and $\text{K}_2\text{FeO}_4$, respectively, are $x, y$ and $z$. The sum of $x, y$ and $z$ is ______.
The incorrect statement is:
options: Manganate and permanganate ions are tetrahedral
In manganate and permanganate ions, the $\pi$-bonding takes place by overlap of $p$-orbitals of oxygen and $d$-orbitals of manganese
Manganate and permanganate ions are paramagnetic
Manganate ion is green in colour and permanganate ion is purple in colour
solution: Manganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$, $\text{Mn}^{6+}: 3d^1$) is paramagnetic with $1$ unpaired electron, whereas permanganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^-$, $\text{Mn}^{7+}: 3d^0$) has no unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic. Thus, statement (C) is incorrect.

question_text:
The incorrect statement(s) among (a) - (c) is (are):
(a) $\text{W}(\text{VI})$ is more stable than $\text{Cr}(\text{VI})$.
(b) In the presence of $\text{HCl}$, permanganate titrations provide satisfactory results.
(c) Some lanthanoid oxides can be used as phosphors.
The correct electronic configuration and spin-only magnetic moment ($\text{BM}$) of $\text{Gd}^{3+}$ ($Z = 64$), respectively, are:
solution: $\text{Gd}^{3+}$ ($Z = 64$) has electronic configuration $[\text{Xe}]4f^7$ with $7$ unpaired electrons. Spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{7(7+2)} = \sqrt{63} = 7.93\text{ BM} \approx 7.9\text{ BM}$.

question_text: The set that contains atomic numbers of only transition elements, is:
solution: Atomic numbers $21$ ($\text{Sc}$), $25$ ($\text{Mn}$), $42$ ($\text{Mo}$), and $72$ ($\text{Hf}$) are all $d$-block transition elements.

question_text: The INCORRECT statement is:
options: bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.
cast iron is used to manufacture wrought iron.
german silver is an alloy of zinc, copper and nickel.
brass is an alloy of copper and nickel.
solution: Brass is an alloy of copper ($\text{Cu}$) and zinc ($\text{Zn}$), not copper and nickel. Thus, statement (D) is incorrect.

question_text: The lanthanoid that does NOT show $+4$ oxidation state is:
solution: $\text{Ce}$, $\text{Tb}$, and $\text{Dy}$ exhibit the $+4$ oxidation state, whereas $\text{Eu}$ ($Z = 63, [\text{Xe}]4f^7 6s^2$) exhibits $+2$ ($4f^7$) and $+3$ ($4f^6$) oxidation states and does not show $+4$.

question_text: Mischmetal is an alloy consisting mainly of:
solution: Mischmetal is a well-known alloy consisting mainly of lanthanoid metals ($\approx 95\%$) and iron ($\approx 5\%$) along with traces of $\text{S}, \text{C}, \text{Ca}$, and $\text{Al}$.

question_text: The electrode potential of $\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}$ of $3d$-series elements shows positive value for:
solution: Copper ($\text{Cu}$) is the only element in the $3d$ transition series with a positive standard reduction potential $E^\circ_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}} = +0.34\text{ V}$, because the high enthalpy of atomisation and sum of first and second ionisation enthalpies of $\text{Cu}$ are not compensated by its hydration enthalpy.

question_text: The major components in "Gun Metal" are:
solution: Gun metal is a type of bronze whose major components are copper ($\text{Cu}, \sim 88\%$), tin ($\text{Sn}, \sim 10\%$), and zinc ($\text{Zn}, \sim 2\%$).

question_text: What is the correct order of the following elements with respect to their density?
solution: Densities (in $\text{g}\cdot\text{cm}^{-3}$): $\text{Zn}$ ($7.1$) $< \text{Cr}$ ($7.19$) $< \text{Fe}$ ($7.87$) $< \text{Co}$ ($8.7$) $< \text{Cu}$ ($8.9$). Thus, $\text{Zn} < \text{Cr} < \text{Fe} < \text{Co} < \text{Cu}$.

question_text: The incorrect statement among the following is:
options: Red colour of ruby is due to the presence of $\text{Co}^{3+}$
solution: The red colour of ruby is due to the presence of $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ions substituting $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ions in octahedral sites of $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, not $\text{Co}^{3+}$. Thus, statement (D) is incorrect.

question_text: In which of the following pairs, the outermost electronic configuration will be the same?
solution:
$\text{Cr}$ ($Z = 24$): $[\text{Ar}]3d^5 4s^1 \implies \text{Cr}^+: [\text{Ar}]3d^5$.
$\text{Mn}$ ($Z = 25$): $[\text{Ar}]3d^5 4s^2 \implies \text{Mn}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}]3d^5$.
Both $\text{Cr}^+$ and $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ have the same outermost configuration $[\text{Ar}]3d^5$.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $\text{CeO}_2$ can be used for oxidation of aldehydes and ketones.
Statement II: Aqueous solution of $\text{EuSO}_4$ is a strong reducing agent.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ in $\text{CeO}_2$ readily gains an electron to revert to the stable $+3$ state ($\text{Ce}^{3+}$), making it a strong oxidising agent for aldehydes and ketones (Statement I is true). $\text{Eu}^{2+}$ in $\text{EuSO}_4$ readily loses an electron to form stable $\text{Eu}^{3+}$, making it a strong reducing agent (Statement II is true).

question_text: The major components of German Silver are:
solution: German silver contains no silver; its major components are copper ($\text{Cu}, \sim 50\%$), zinc ($\text{Zn}, \sim 30\%$), and nickel ($\text{Ni}, \sim 20\%$).

question_text: Which one of the following lanthanoids does not form $\text{MO}_2$? [$\text{M}$ is lanthanoid metal]
solution: $\text{Pr}$, $\text{Nd}$, and $\text{Dy}$ form dioxides ($\text{MO}_2$), whereas ytterbium ($\text{Yb}, [\text{Xe}]4f^{14}6s^2$) does not form $\text{MO}_2$ because $+4$ oxidation state would disrupt its completely filled $4f^{14}$ shell.

question_text: Dichromate ion is treated with base, the oxidation number of $\text{Cr}$ in the product formed is ______.
solution: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 2\text{OH}^- \longrightarrow 2\text{CrO}_4^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. In the chromate ion ($\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$), the oxidation number of $\text{Cr}$ remains $+6$.

question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R:
Assertion A: Size of $\text{Bk}^{3+}$ ion is less than $\text{Np}^{3+}$ ion.
Reason R: The above is a consequence of the lanthanide contraction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
solution: The ionic radius of $\text{Bk}^{3+}$ ($Z = 97$) is smaller than that of $\text{Np}^{3+}$ ($Z = 93$) (Assertion A is true), which is a consequence of actinoid contraction (poor shielding by $5f$ electrons), not lanthanide contraction (Reason R is false).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
solution: $2\text{KMnO}_4 \xrightarrow{573\text{ K}} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2\uparrow$ (Statement I is true). question_text: In the ground state of atomic $\text{Fe}$ ($Z = 26$), the spin-only magnetic moment is ______ $\times 10^{-1}\text{ BM}$. (Round off to the Nearest Integer) [Given: $\sqrt{3} = 1.73, \sqrt{2} = 1.41$]
solution: $\text{Fe}$ ($Z = 26$): $[\text{Ar}]3d^6 4s^2$, which has $n = 4$ unpaired electrons in the $3d$ subshell. $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6} = 2 \times 1.73 \times 1.41 = 4.88\text{ BM} = 48.8 \times 10^{-1}\text{ BM} \approx 49 \times 10^{-1}\text{ BM}$.

question_text: The common positive oxidation states for an element with atomic number $24$, are:
solution: The element with atomic number $24$ is chromium ($\text{Cr}, [\text{Ar}]3d^5 4s^1$), whose common positive oxidation states range from $+2$ to $+6$ ($+2, +3, +4, +5, +6$).

The set having ions which are coloured and paramagnetic both is:
solution: $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^9$, $1$ unpaired $e^-$), $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^3$, $3$ unpaired $e^-$), and $\text{Sc}^+$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^1 4s^1$, $2$ unpaired $e^-$) all possess unpaired $d$-electrons and are both coloured and paramagnetic.

Number of electrons present in $4f$ orbital of $\text{Ho}^{3+}$ ion is ______ (Given Atomic No. of $\text{Ho} = 67$).
solution: Holmium ($Z = 67$) has the ground-state electronic configuration $[\text{Xe}]4f^{11}6s^2$. Removing three electrons gives $\text{Ho}^{3+}: [\text{Xe}]4f^{10}$, which contains $10$ electrons in the $4f$ orbital.

question_text: The spin only magnetic moments (in $\text{BM}$) for free $\text{Ti}^{3+}$, $\text{V}^{2+}$ and $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ ions respectively are (At. No. $\text{Sc}: 21, \text{Ti}: 22, \text{V}: 23$):
Which one of the following when dissolved in water gives coloured solution in nitrogen atmosphere?
solution: $\text{CuCl}_2$ dissolves in water to give hydrated $\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq)$ ($3d^9$, $1$ unpaired electron), which forms a blue-coloured solution. $\text{AgCl}$ and $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2$ are insoluble in water, and $\text{ZnCl}_2$ ($\text{Zn}^{2+}, 3d^{10}$) forms a colourless solution.

question_text: The number of $4f$ electrons in the ground state electronic configuration of $\text{Gd}^{2+}$ is ______ [Atomic number of $\text{Gd} = 64$].
solution: Electronic configuration of $\text{Gd}$ ($Z = 64$) is $[\text{Xe}]4f^7 5d^1 6s^2$. Removing the two $6s$ electrons gives $\text{Gd}^{2+}: [\text{Xe}]4f^7 5d^1$, which has $7$ electrons in the $4f$ orbital.

question_text: The nature of oxides $\text{V}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{CrO}$ is indexed as '$\text{X}$' and '$\text{Y}$' type respectively. The correct set of $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ is:
solution: Lower-oxidation-state transition metal oxides such as $\text{V}_2\text{O}_3$ ($+3$) and $\text{CrO}$ ($+2$) are predominantly ionic and basic in nature. Thus, $\text{X} = \text{basic}$ and $\text{Y} = \text{basic}$.

question_text: In Carius method for estimation of halogens, $0.2\text{ g}$ of an organic compound gave $0.188\text{ g}$ of $\text{AgBr}$. The percentage of bromine in the compound is ______ (Nearest integer) [Atomic mass: $\text{Ag} = 108, \text{Br} = 80$].
solution: Percentage of $\text{Br} = \frac{\text{Atomic mass of Br}}{\text{Molecular mass of AgBr}} \times \frac{\text{Mass of AgBr}}{\text{Mass of compound}} \times 100 = \frac{80}{188} \times \frac{0.188}{0.2} \times 100 = 40\%$.

question_text: The number of $f$ electrons in the ground state electronic configuration of $\text{Np}$ ($Z = 93$) is ______ (integer answer).
solution: Neptunium ($Z = 93$) has the electronic configuration $[\text{Rn}]5f^4 6d^1 7s^2$, where $[\text{Rn}]$ includes a completely filled $4f^{14}$ subshell. Total number of $f$ electrons $= 14\text{ (in } 4f) + 4\text{ (in } 5f) = 18$.

question_text: Potassium permanganate on heating at $513\text{ K}$ gives a product which is:
solution: $2\text{KMnO}_4 \xrightarrow{513\text{ K}} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 + \text{MnO}_2(s) + \text{O}_2(g)$. Potassium manganate ($\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$, containing $\text{Mn}^{6+}$ with $3d^1$ configuration) is green in colour and paramagnetic.

question_text: Which one of the following is used to remove most of plutonium from spent nuclear fuel?
solution: Dioxygen difluoride ($\text{O}_2\text{F}_2$) oxidises plutonium to volatile $\text{PuF}_6$, and this reaction is used to remove plutonium as $\text{PuF}_6$ from spent nuclear fuel.

question_text: In the structure of the dichromate ion, there is a:
solution: The dichromate ion ($\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$) consists of two $\text{CrO}_4$ tetrahedra sharing one corner oxygen atom with a bent (non-linear) symmetrical $\text{Cr}-\text{O}-\text{Cr}$ bridge (bond angle $126^\circ$ and equal bridging $\text{Cr}-\text{O}$ bond lengths of $179\text{ pm}$).

question_text: Which one of the following lanthanides exhibits $+2$ oxidation state with diamagnetic nature? (Given $Z$ for $\text{Nd} = 60, \text{Yb} = 70, \text{La} = 57, \text{Ce} = 58$)
solution: Ytterbium ($Z = 70$) has configuration $[\text{Xe}]4f^{14}6s^2$, so $\text{Yb}^{2+}$ has a completely filled $4f^{14}$ configuration with zero unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic.

question_text: The $\text{Eu}^{2+}$ ion is a strong reducing agent in spite of its ground state electronic configuration (outermost): [Atomic number of $\text{Eu} = 63$]
solution: $\text{Eu}$ ($Z = 63$) has configuration $[\text{Xe}]4f^7 6s^2$, so $\text{Eu}^{2+}$ has the half-filled outermost configuration $[\text{Xe}]4f^7$, yet it still acts as a strong reducing agent by oxidising to the common $+3$ lanthanoid state ($\text{Eu}^{3+}$).

question_text: Identify the element for which electronic configuration in $+3$ oxidation state is $[\text{Ar}]3d^5$:
solution: If $\text{M}^{3+} = [\text{Ar}]3d^5$, the neutral atom $\text{M}$ has $18 + 5 + 3 = 26$ electrons, which corresponds to Iron ($\text{Fe}, [\text{Ar}]3d^6 4s^2$).

question_text:
In the given chemical reaction, colors of the $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions, are respectively:
$5\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ \longrightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} + 5\text{Fe}^{3+}$
solution: In aqueous solution, hydrated $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($3d^6$) is pale green in colour, whereas $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($3d^5$) is yellow/yellow-brown in colour.

question_text: The difference in oxidation state of chromium in chromate and dichromate salts is ______.
solution: In both chromate ($\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$) and dichromate ($\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$), chromium is in the $+6$ oxidation state. Therefore, the difference in oxidation state is $6 - 6 = 0$.

question_text: Among the following, which is the strongest oxidizing agent?
solution: Standard reduction potentials ($E^\circ_{\text{M}^{3+}/\text{M}^{2+}}$): $\text{Mn}^{3+}/\text{Mn}^{2+} = +1.57\text{ V}$, $\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+} = +0.77\text{ V}$, $\text{Ti}^{3+}/\text{Ti}^{2+} = -0.37\text{ V}$, $\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}^{2+} = -0.41\text{ V}$. Because $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ ($3d^4$) readily gains an electron to attain the stable half-filled $3d^5$ configuration of $\text{Mn}^{2+}$, it has the highest reduction potential and is the strongest oxidising agent.

question_text: Cerium(IV) has a noble gas configuration. Which of the following is correct statement about it?
options: It will prefer to gain electron and act as an oxidizing agent.
It will prefer to give away an electron and behave as reducing agent.
It will not prefer to undergo redox reactions.
It acts as both, oxidizing and reducing agent.
solution: Although $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ has a noble-gas configuration ($[\text{Xe}]4f^0$), $+3$ is the most stable oxidation state for lanthanoids in aqueous solution ($E^\circ_{\text{Ce}^{4+}/\text{Ce}^{3+}} = +1.74\text{ V}$). Thus, $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ strongly prefers to gain an electron to revert to $\text{Ce}^{3+}$ and acts as a strong oxidising agent.

question_text: The metal ion (in gaseous state) with lowest spin-only magnetic moment value is:
solution: Number of unpaired electrons: $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($3d^4 \to 4$), $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($3d^6 \to 4$), $\text{V}^{2+}$ ($3d^3 \to 3$), and $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($3d^8 \to 2$). Since $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ has the fewest unpaired electrons ($n = 2$), it has the lowest spin-only magnetic moment ($\sqrt{8} = 2.83\text{ BM}$).

question_text: The spin-only magnetic moment value of the most basic oxide of vanadium among $\text{V}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_4$ and $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ is ______ $\text{BM}$. (Nearest integer)

(D) $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ reduces the persulphate ion
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
solution:
The catalytic cycle proceeds in two steps:
Step 1: $2\text{Fe}^{3+} + 2\text{I}^- \longrightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{I}_2$ ($\text{Fe}^{3+}$ oxidises iodide ion, A is correct).
Step 2: $2\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-} \longrightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{3+} + 2\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ($\text{Fe}^{2+}$ reduces persulphate ion, D is correct).
Thus, A and D only.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Fusion of $\text{MnO}_2$ with $\text{KOH}$ and an oxidising agent gives dark green $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$.
Statement (II): Manganate ion on electrolytic oxidation in alkaline medium gives permanganate ion.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
solution:
Statement I: $2\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{KOH} + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{fused}} 2\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4\text{ (dark green)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (True).
Statement II: Electrolytic oxidation in alkaline medium converts manganate to permanganate at the anode: $\text{MnO}_4^{2-} \longrightarrow \text{MnO}_4^- + e^-$ (True).
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

question_text: Electronic configuration of $\text{Cu}(\text{II})$ is $3d^9$ whereas that of $\text{Cu}(\text{I})$ is $3d^{10}$. Which of the following is correct?
options: Stability of $\text{Cu}(\text{I})$ and $\text{Cu}(\text{II})$ depends on nature of copper salts
solution: $\text{Cu}(\text{II})$ is more stable than $\text{Cu}(\text{I})$ in aqueous solution because the much higher negative hydration enthalpy of $\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq)$ compared to $\text{Cu}^+(aq)$ more than compensates for the second ionisation enthalpy of copper.

question_text: $0.05\text{ M } \text{CuSO}_4$ when treated with $0.01\text{ M } \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ gives green colour solution of $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$. The two solutions are separated by a semi-permeable membrane (SPM): Side X ($0.01\text{ M } \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$) | SPM | Side Y ($0.05\text{ M } \text{CuSO}_4$). Due to osmosis:
options: Green colour formation observed on side Y.
Green colour formation observed on side X.
solution: A semi-permeable membrane allows only solvent (water) molecules to pass through, so no solute ions cross and no green $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ forms on either side. Water flows by osmosis from the more dilute solution (Side X, $0.01\text{ M } \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$) to the more concentrated solution (Side Y, $0.05\text{ M } \text{CuSO}_4$), lowering the molarity of the $\text{CuSO}_4$ solution.

question_text:
Number of colourless lanthanoid ions among the following is ______:
$\text{Eu}^{3+}, \text{Lu}^{3+}, \text{Nd}^{3+}, \text{La}^{3+}, \text{Sm}^{3+}$
solution: $\text{La}^{3+}$ ($[\text{Xe}]4f^0$) and $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ ($[\text{Xe}]4f^{14}$) have no unpaired $4f$ electrons and are colourless ($2$ ions), whereas $\text{Nd}^{3+}$ ($4f^3$), $\text{Sm}^{3+}$ ($4f^5$), and $\text{Eu}^{3+}$ ($4f^6$) are coloured.

question_text:
A transition metal '$\text{M}$' among $\text{Sc}, \text{Ti}, \text{V}, \text{Cr}, \text{Mn}$ and $\text{Fe}$ has the highest second ionisation enthalpy. The spin-only magnetic moment value of $\text{M}^+$ ion is ______ $\text{BM}$ (Near integer)
(Given atomic number $\text{Sc}: 21, \text{Ti}: 22, \text{V}: 23, \text{Cr}: 24, \text{Mn}: 25, \text{Fe}: 26$)
solution: Among the given elements, $\text{Cr}$ ($Z = 24$) has the highest second ionisation enthalpy because the second electron is removed from the extra-stable half-filled configuration $\text{Cr}^+: [\text{Ar}]3d^5 4s^0$. With $n = 5$ unpaired electrons in $\text{Cr}^+$, $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} = 5.92\text{ BM} \approx 6\text{ BM}$.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The higher oxidation states are more stable down the group among transition elements unlike $p$-block elements.
Statement II: Copper cannot liberate hydrogen from weak acids.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
solution: In transition element groups, higher oxidation states become more stable down the group (e.g., $\text{W}(\text{VI}) > \text{Mo}(\text{VI}) > \text{Cr}(\text{VI})$), opposite to $p$-block elements where lower states are favoured by the inert pair effect (Statement I is true). Because $E^\circ_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}} = +0.34\text{ V} > E^\circ_{\text{H}^+/\text{H}_2} = 0.00\text{ V}$, copper cannot liberate $\text{H}_2$ from weak acids (Statement II is true).

question_text: The electronic configuration of Einsteinium is (Given atomic number of Einsteinium $= 99$):
solution: Einsteinium ($\text{Es}$, atomic number $Z = 99$) has the ground-state electronic configuration $[\text{Rn}]5f^{11} 6d^0 7s^2$.

question_text:
Lanthanoid ions with $4f^7$ configuration are:
(A) $\text{Eu}^{2+}$
(B) $\text{Gd}^{3+}$
(C) $\text{Eu}^{3+}$
(D) $\text{Tb}^{3+}$
(E) $\text{Sm}^{2+}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution:
Electronic configurations:
(A) $_{63}\text{Eu}^{2+}: [\text{Xe}]4f^7$
(B) $_{64}\text{Gd}^{3+}: [\text{Xe}]4f^7$
(C) $_{63}\text{Eu}^{3+}: [\text{Xe}]4f^6$
(D) $_{65}\text{Tb}^{3+}: [\text{Xe}]4f^8$
(E) $_{62}\text{Sm}^{2+}: [\text{Xe}]4f^6$
Thus, (A) and (B) only have a $4f^7$ configuration.

question_text: Niobium ($\text{Nb}$) and ruthenium ($\text{Ru}$) have '$x$' and '$y$' number of electrons in their respective $4d$ orbitals. The value of $x + y$ is ______.
solution:
$\text{Nb}$ ($Z = 41$): $[\text{Kr}]4d^4 5s^1 \implies x = 4$ electrons in $4d$.
$\text{Ru}$ ($Z = 44$): $[\text{Kr}]4d^7 5s^1 \implies y = 7$ electrons in $4d$.
$x + y = 4 + 7 = 11$.

question_text: The correct set of ions (aqueous solution) with same colour from the following is:
solution: In aqueous solution, $\text{V}^{2+}$ ($3d^3$), $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($3d^3$), and $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ ($3d^4$) all exhibit a violet colour.

question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Alloy): (A) Bronze, (B) Brass, (C) UK silver coin, (D) Stainless steel
List-II (Composition): (I) $\text{Cu}, \text{Ni}$, (II) $\text{Fe}, \text{Cr}, \text{Ni}, \text{C}$, (III) $\text{Cu}, \text{Zn}$, (IV) $\text{Cu}, \text{Sn}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Consider the following reactions:
$\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 \xrightarrow[-\text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{KOH}} [\text{A}] \xrightarrow[-\text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} [\text{B}] + \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4$
The products $[\text{A}]$ and $[\text{B}]$, respectively are:
solution: In alkaline medium, dichromate converts to yellow chromate ($[\text{A}] = \text{K}_2\text{CrO}_4$): $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 2\text{KOH} \longrightarrow 2\text{K}_2\text{CrO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Upon acidification with $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, chromate reverts to orange dichromate ($[\text{B}] = \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$): $2\text{K}_2\text{CrO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Bronze, (B) Brass, (C) UK silver coin, (D) Stainless steel
List-II: (I) $\text{Cu}, \text{Ni}$, (II) $\text{Fe}, \text{Cr}, \text{Ni}, \text{C}$, (III) $\text{Cu}, \text{Zn}$, (IV) $\text{Cu}, \text{Sn}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: (A) Bronze: $\text{Cu}, \text{Sn}$ (IV); (B) Brass: $\text{Cu}, \text{Zn}$ (III); (C) UK silver coin: $\text{Cu}, \text{Ni}$ (I); (D) Stainless steel: $\text{Fe}, \text{Cr}, \text{Ni}, \text{C}$ (II).

question_text: Preparation of potassium permanganate from $\text{MnO}_2$ involves two-step process in which the $1^{\text{st}}$ step is a reaction with $\text{KOH}$ and $\text{KNO}_3$ to produce:
solution: In the first step, pyrolusite ($\text{MnO}_2$) is fused with $\text{KOH}$ and an oxidising agent like $\text{KNO}_3$ to produce dark green potassium manganate ($\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$): $\text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{KOH} + \text{KNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 + \text{KNO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

question_text:
Which of the following ions is the strongest oxidizing agent?
(Atomic Number of $\text{Ce} = 58, \text{Eu} = 63, \text{Tb} = 65, \text{Lu} = 71$)
solution: $\text{Tb}^{4+}$ ($[\text{Xe}]4f^7$) has a strong tendency to gain an electron and revert to the common $+3$ lanthanoid state ($\text{Tb}^{3+}$), making it a very strong oxidising agent ($\text{Eu}^{2+}$ is a reducing agent, while $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ and $\text{Ce}^{3+}$ are already in the stable $+3$ state).

question_text:
Find the compound '$\text{A}$' from the following reaction sequence:
$\text{A} \xrightarrow{\text{aqua regia}} \text{B} \xrightarrow[(2)\;\text{AcOH}]{(1)\;\text{KNO}_2 / \text{NH}_4\text{OH}} \text{yellow ppt}$
solution: Black cobalt(II) sulphide ($\text{CoS}$, compound $\text{A}$) dissolves in aqua regia to form $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ($\text{B}$). Upon neutralisation with $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ and addition of $\text{KNO}_2$ in acetic acid, $\text{Co}^{2+}$ is oxidised to $\text{Co}^{3+}$ and precipitates as yellow potassium hexanitritocobaltate(III), $\text{K}_3[\text{Co}(\text{NO}_2)_6]$.

question_text:
Consider '$n$' is the number of lone pairs of electrons present in the equatorial position of the most stable structure of $\text{ClF}_3$. The ions from the following with '$n$' number of unpaired electrons are:

(D) $\text{Ni}^{2+}$
(E) $\text{Ti}^{2+}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Which of the following oxidation reactions are carried out by both $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ and $\text{KMnO}_4$ in acidic medium?
(A) $\text{I}^- \longrightarrow \text{I}_2$
(B) $\text{S}^{2-} \longrightarrow \text{S}$
(C) $\text{Fe}^{2+} \longrightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+}$
(D) $\text{I}^- \longrightarrow \text{IO}_3^-$
(E) $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \longrightarrow \text{SO}_4^{2-}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: In acidic medium, both $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ and $\text{KMnO}_4$ oxidise $\text{I}^-$ to $\text{I}_2$ (A), $\text{S}^{2-}$ to $\text{S}$ (B), and $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ (C). Oxidation of $\text{I}^-$ to $\text{IO}_3^-$ (D) and quantitative oxidation of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$ to $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ (E) occur with $\text{KMnO}_4$ in neutral/faintly alkaline medium. Thus, A, B and C Only.

question_text: The spin only magnetic moment ($\mu$) value ($\text{BM}$) of the compound with strongest oxidising power among $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{TiO}$ and $\text{VO}$ is ______ $\text{BM}$. (Nearest integer)
solution: Among $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{TiO}$, and $\text{VO}$, $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_3$ has the strongest oxidising power ($E^\circ_{\text{Mn}^{3+}/\text{Mn}^{2+}} = +1.57\text{ V}$, as $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ reduces to half-filled $3d^5$ $\text{Mn}^{2+}$). In $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^4$) has $n = 4$ unpaired electrons, giving $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} = 4.90\text{ BM} \approx 5\text{ BM}$.

question_text: The amphoteric oxide among $\text{V}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_4$ and $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$, upon reaction with alkali leads to formation of an oxide anion. The oxidation state of $\text{V}$ in the oxide anion is:
solution: $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ is amphoteric and dissolves in alkali to give orthovanadate ($	ext{VO}_4^{3-}$) / metavanadate ($	ext{VO}_3^-$), in which vanadium remains in the $+5$ oxidation state.

question_text:
Identify the inorganic sulphides that are yellow in colour:
(A) $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{S}$
(B) $\text{PbS}$
(C) $\text{CuS}$
(D) $\text{As}_2\text{S}_3$
(E) $\text{As}_2\text{S}_5$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: $\text{As}_2\text{S}_3$ and $\text{As}_2\text{S}_5$ are yellow-coloured precipitates, whereas $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{S}$ is a colourless solution and $\text{PbS}$ and $\text{CuS}$ are black precipitates (note: official NTA answer key lists B, (D) and (E) only).

question_text: The molar mass of the water insoluble product formed from the fusion of chromite ore ($\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4$) with $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ in presence of $\text{O}_2$ is ______ $\text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$.
solution: $4\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4 + 8\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 7\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow 8\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4 + 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + 8\text{CO}_2$. The water-insoluble product is $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$, whose molar mass $= 2(56) + 3(16) = 112 + 48 = 160\text{ g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$.

question_text: The correct option with order of melting points of the pairs $(\text{Mn}, \text{Fe})$, $(\text{Tc}, \text{Ru})$ and $(\text{Re}, \text{Os})$ is:
solution: Due to the anomalously low melting points of $\text{Mn}$ ($1519\text{ K}$) and $\text{Tc}$ ($2430\text{ K}$) resulting from their half-filled $d^5$ stability (weaker metallic bonding), $\text{Mn} < \text{Fe}$ ($1811\text{ K}$) and $\text{Tc} < \text{Ru}$ ($2607\text{ K}$), whereas in the $5d$ series $\text{Re}$ ($3459\text{ K}$) has a higher melting point than $\text{Os}$ ($3306\text{ K}$), so $\text{Os} < \text{Re}$.

Among $\text{Sc}, \text{Mn}, \text{Co}$ and $\text{Cu}$, identify the element with highest enthalpy of atomisation. The spin only magnetic moment value of that element in its $+2$ oxidation state is ______ $\text{BM}$ (in nearest integer).
solution: Enthalpies of atomisation: $\text{Sc}$ ($326\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$), $\text{Mn}$ ($281\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$), $\text{Co}$ ($425\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$), and $\text{Cu}$ ($339\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$). Cobalt ($\text{Co}$) has the highest enthalpy of atomisation. $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^7$) has $n = 3$ unpaired electrons, giving $\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} = 3.87\text{ BM} \approx 4\text{ BM}$.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $\text{CrO}_3$ is a stronger oxidizing agent than $\text{MoO}_3$.
Statement II: $\text{Cr}(\text{VI})$ is more stable than $\text{Mo}(\text{VI})$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
solution: In Group 6, the stability of the $+6$ oxidation state increases down the group ($\text{Cr}(\text{VI}) < \text{Mo}(\text{VI}) < \text{W}(\text{VI})$), so $\text{Cr}(\text{VI})$ is less stable than $\text{Mo}(\text{VI})$ (Statement II is false) and $\text{CrO}_3$ is a much stronger oxidising agent than $\text{MoO}_3$ (Statement I is true).

question_text: Pair of transition metal ions having the same number of unpaired electrons is:
solution: $\text{V}^{2+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^3$) has $3$ unpaired electrons, and $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^7$) also has $3$ unpaired electrons.

question_text: $\text{KMnO}_4$ acts as an oxidising agent in acidic medium. '$\text{X}$' is the difference between the oxidation states of $\text{Mn}$ in reactant and product. '$\text{Y}$' is the number of '$d$' electrons present in the brown red precipitate formed at the end of the acetate ion test with neutral ferric chloride. The value of $\text{X} + \text{Y}$ is ______.
solution:
In acidic medium, $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ($+7$) is reduced to $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($+2$), so $\text{X} = 7 - 2 = 5$.
In the acetate ion test with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$, boiling the deep red solution yields a brownish-red precipitate of basic iron(III) acetate, $[\text{Fe}(\text{OH})_2(\text{CH}_3\text{COO})]$, where $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^5$) has $\text{Y} = 5$ $d$-electrons.
Thus, $\text{X} + \text{Y} = 5 + 5 = 10$.

question_text: The incorrect relationship in the following pairs in relation to ionisation enthalpies is:
solution: The third ionisation enthalpy of $\text{Mn}$ (removing an electron from half-filled $\text{Mn}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}]3d^5$, $3248\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) is greater than that of $\text{Fe}$ (removing an electron from $\text{Fe}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}]3d^6$ to achieve stable $3d^5$, $2957\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$). Hence, $\text{Mn}^{2+} > \text{Fe}^{2+}$, making option (D) incorrect.

question_text: The first transition series metal '$\text{M}$' has the highest enthalpy of atomisation in its series. One of its aquated ions ($\text{M}^{n+}$) exists in green colour. The nature of the oxide formed by the above $\text{M}^{n+}$ ion is:
solution: Vanadium ($\text{V}$) has the highest enthalpy of atomisation ($515\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) in the $3d$ series, and its aquated ion $\text{V}^{3+}(aq)$ is green in colour. The corresponding oxide $\text{V}_2\text{O}_3$ is basic in nature.

question_text: The number of valence electrons present in the metal among $\text{Cr}, \text{Co}, \text{Fe}$ and $\text{Ni}$ which has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation is:
solution: Enthalpies of atomisation: $\text{Cr}$ ($397\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$), $\text{Fe}$ ($416\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$), $\text{Co}$ ($425\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$), $\text{Ni}$ ($430\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$). Chromium ($\text{Cr}, [\text{Ar}]3d^5 4s^1$) has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation among these four metals and has $5 + 1 = 6$ valence electrons.

question_text: '$X$' is the number of acidic oxides among $\text{VO}_2$, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{CrO}_3$, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ and $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$. The primary valency of cobalt in $[\text{Co}(\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2)_3]_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$ is $Y$. The value of $X + Y$ is:
solution: Among $\text{VO}_2$ (amphoteric), $\text{V}_2\text{O}_3$ (basic), $\text{CrO}_3$ (acidic), $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ (amphoteric), and $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$ (acidic), there are $X = 2$ purely acidic oxides ($\text{CrO}_3$ and $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$). In $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$, the oxidation state (primary valency) of cobalt is $Y = +3$. Thus, $X + Y = 2 + 3 = 5$.

question_text: The correct decreasing order of spin only magnetic moment values ($\text{BM}$) of $\text{Cu}^+$, $\text{Cu}^{2+}$, $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ions is:
solution: Number of unpaired electrons ($n$): $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($3d^4 \to 4$), $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($3d^3 \to 3$), $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ($3d^9 \to 1$), $\text{Cu}^+$ ($3d^{10} \to 0$). Therefore, the spin-only magnetic moments decrease in the order $\text{Cr}^{2+} > \text{Cr}^{3+} > \text{Cu}^{2+} > \text{Cu}^+$.

question_text: $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$, in acidic medium, disproportionates to:
solution: In acidic or neutral medium, manganate ion ($\text{Mn}^{6+}$) disproportionates into permanganate ($\text{Mn}^{7+}$) and manganese dioxide ($\text{Mn}^{4+}$): $3\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ \longrightarrow 2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

question_text:
Consider the following reactions:
$\text{NaCl} + \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \text{A} + \text{KHSO}_4 + \text{NaHSO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
$\text{A} + \text{NaOH} \longrightarrow \text{B} + \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
$\text{B} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow \text{C} + \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
In the product '$\text{C}$', '$X$' is the number of $\text{O}_2^{2-}$ units, '$Y$' is the total number of oxygen atoms present and '$Z$' is the oxidation state of $\text{Cr}$. The value of $X + Y + Z$ is ______.
solution: $\text{A} = \text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{B} = \text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4$, and $\text{C} = \text{CrO}_5$ ($\text{CrO}(\text{O}_2)_2$, butterfly structure with one oxo ligand and two peroxo $\text{O}_2^{2-}$ units). Thus, $X = 2$, $Y = 5$, and $Z = +6$, giving $X + Y + Z = 2 + 5 + 6 = 13$.

question_text:
Given below are some of the statements about $\text{Mn}$ and $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$. Identify the correct statements:
(A) $\text{Mn}$ forms the oxide $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$ in which $\text{Mn}$ is in its highest oxidation state.
(B) Oxygen stabilizes the $\text{Mn}$ in higher oxidation states by forming multiple bonds with $\text{Mn}$.
(C) $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$ is an ionic oxide.
(D) The structure of $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$ consists of one bridged oxygen.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

On heating a mixture of common salt and $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ in equal amount along with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in a test tube, a gas is evolved. Formula of the gas evolved and oxidation state of the central metal atom in the gas respectively are:
solution: $4\text{NaCl} + \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 6\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2\uparrow + 2\text{KHSO}_4 + 4\text{NaHSO}_4 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The evolved red-brown gas is chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$), in which chromium is in the $+6$ oxidation state.

question_text: A first row transition metal ($\text{M}$) does not liberate $\text{H}_2$ gas from dilute $\text{HCl}$. $1\text{ mol}$ of aqueous solution of $\text{MSO}_4$ is treated with excess of aqueous $\text{KCN}$ and then $\text{H}_2\text{S}(g)$ is passed through the solution. The amount of $\text{MS}$ (metal sulphide) formed from the above reaction is ______ $\text{mol}$.
solution: The metal $\text{M}$ is $\text{Cu}$ ($E^\circ_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}} = +0.34\text{ V}$). Reaction of $\text{CuSO}_4$ with excess $\text{KCN}$ yields the extremely stable soluble tetracyanocuprate(I) complex $\text{K}_3[\text{Cu}(\text{CN})_4]$, which provides negligible free $\text{Cu}^+$ ions in solution. Passing $\text{H}_2\text{S}(g)$ therefore gives no sulphide precipitate ($0\text{ mol}$).

question_text:
Among the following oxides of $3d$ elements, the number of mixed oxides is ______:
$\text{Ti}_2\text{O}_3, \text{V}_2\text{O}_4, \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3, \text{Mn}_3\text{O}_4, \text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4, \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3, \text{Co}_3\text{O}_4$
solution:
Mixed oxides contain the same metal in two different oxidation states:
$\text{Mn}_3\text{O}_4$ ($\text{MnO}\cdot \text{Mn}_2\text{O}_3$, $+2$ and $+3$),
$\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$ ($\text{FeO}\cdot \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$, $+2$ and $+3$),
and $\text{Co}_3\text{O}_4$ ($\text{CoO}\cdot \text{Co}_2\text{O}_3$, $+2$ and $+3$).
Thus, there are $3$ mixed oxides.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The first ionization enthalpy of $\text{Cr}$ is lower than that of $\text{Mn}$.
Statement II: The second and third ionization enthalpies of $\text{Cr}$ are higher than those of $\text{Mn}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
solution:
Statement I: $\text{IE}_1$ of $\text{Cr}$ ($653\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$, removing $4s^1$) is lower than $\text{IE}_1$ of $\text{Mn}$ ($717\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$, removing from filled $4s^2$) (True).
Statement II: $\text{IE}_2$ of $\text{Cr}$ ($1592\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$, from $3d^5$) is higher than $\text{IE}_2$ of $\text{Mn}$ ($1509\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$), but $\text{IE}_3$ of $\text{Cr}$ ($2987\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$, from $3d^4$) is lower than $\text{IE}_3$ of $\text{Mn}$ ($3248\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$, from half-filled $3d^5$) (False).
Thus, Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

question_text: The oxidation state of chromium in the final product formed in the reaction between $\text{KI}$ and acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ solution is:
solution: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6\text{I}^- \longrightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3\text{I}_2$. Chromium is reduced from $+6$ in dichromate to $+3$ ($\text{Cr}^{3+}$) in the final product.

question_text: '$\text{X}$' is an oxoanion of the lightest element of group $7$ (in the periodic table). The metal is in $+6$ oxidation state in '$\text{X}$'. The color of the potassium salt of $\text{X}$ is:
solution: The lightest Group 7 transition element is manganese ($\text{Mn}$), and its oxoanion in the $+6$ oxidation state is manganate ($\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$). Its potassium salt, potassium manganate ($\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$), is dark green in colour.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The number of pairs, from the following, in which both the ions are coloured in aqueous solution is $3$:
$[\text{Sc}^{3+}, \text{Ti}^{3+}]$, $[\text{Mn}^{2+}, \text{Cr}^{2+}]$, $[\text{Cu}^{2+}, \text{Zn}^{2+}]$ and $[\text{Ni}^{2+}, \text{Ti}^{4+}]$
Statement II: $\text{Th}^{4+}$ is the strongest reducing agent among $\text{Th}^{4+}$, $\text{Ce}^{4+}$, $\text{Gd}^{3+}$ and $\text{Eu}^{2+}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
solution:
Statement I: $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ ($3d^0$), $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ($3d^{10}$), and $\text{Ti}^{4+}$ ($3d^0$) are colourless in aqueous solution, so none of the pairs have both ions coloured (False).
Statement II: $\text{Th}^{4+}$ ($[\text{Rn}]5f^0$) is in its highest stable oxidation state and cannot act as a reducing agent, whereas $\text{Eu}^{2+}$ ($[\text{Xe}]4f^7$) is the strongest reducing agent among the four (False).
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

(A) The geometry of both manganate and permanganate ions is tetrahedral.
(B) The oxidation states of $\text{Mn}$ in manganate and permanganate are $+7$ and $+6$, respectively.
(C) Oxidation of $\text{Mn}(\text{II})$ salt by peroxodisulphate gives manganate ion as the final product.
(D) Manganate ion is paramagnetic and permanganate ion is diamagnetic.
(E) Acidified permanganate ion reduces oxalate, nitrite and iodide ions.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
Which of the following sets includes all the species that will change the orange colour of $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ in acidic medium?
solution: Acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ changes from orange ($\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$) to green ($\text{Cr}^{3+}$) only when all species in the set can act as reducing agents. In option (A), $\text{Fe}^{2+} \to \text{Fe}^{3+}$, $\text{Sn}^{2+} \to \text{Sn}^{4+}$, $\text{I}^- \to \text{I}_2$, and $\text{S}^{2-} \to \text{S}$ are all reducing agents (whereas $\text{Fe}^{3+}$, $\text{Sn}^{4+}$, and $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ in the other options are already in their maximum oxidation states).

question_text:
Number of paramagnetic ions among the following $d$- and $f$-block metal ions is ______:
$\text{Mn}^{2+}, \text{Cu}^{2+}, \text{Zn}^{2+}, \text{Yb}^{2+}, \text{Sc}^{3+}, \text{La}^{3+}, \text{Gd}^{3+}, \text{Lu}^{3+}, \text{Ti}^{4+}, \text{Ce}^{4+}$
(Atomic number of $\text{Mn} = 25, \text{Cu} = 29, \text{Zn} = 30, \text{Yb} = 70, \text{Sc} = 21, \text{La} = 57, \text{Gd} = 64, \text{Lu} = 71, \text{Ti} = 22, \text{Ce} = 58$)
solution:
Paramagnetic ions (having unpaired electrons):
$\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^5 \to 5$ unpaired $e^-$),
$\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^9 \to 1$ unpaired $e^-$),
$\text{Gd}^{3+}$ ($[\text{Xe}]4f^7 \to 7$ unpaired $e^-$).
Diamagnetic ions ($0$ unpaired electrons): $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ($3d^{10}$), $\text{Yb}^{2+}$ ($4f^{14}$), $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ ($3d^0$), $\text{La}^{3+}$ ($4f^0$), $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ ($4f^{14}$), $\text{Ti}^{4+}$ ($3d^0$), $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ ($4f^0$). Total paramagnetic ions $= 3$.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Presence of large number of unpaired electrons in transition metal atoms results in higher enthalpies of their atomisation.
Statement II: $d_{xy} = d_{xz} = d_{yz} < d_{x^2-y^2} = d_{z^2}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2} = d_{z^2} < d_{xy} = d_{xz} = d_{yz}$ are the $d$-orbital splittings in $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ and $[\text{Ni}(\text{Cl})_4]^{2-}$ complex ions respectively.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution:
Statement I: More unpaired $d$-electrons enable stronger interatomic metallic bonding, giving higher enthalpies of atomisation (True).
Statement II: $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ is octahedral ($t_{2g} < e_g$, so $d_{xy} = d_{xz} = d_{yz} < d_{x^2-y^2} = d_{z^2}$) and $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is tetrahedral ($e < t_2$, so $d_{x^2-y^2} = d_{z^2} < d_{xy} = d_{xz} = d_{yz}$) (True).
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

question_text: A paper dipped in a dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution of '$\text{X}$' upon treatment with $\text{SO}_2$ gas turns into green. The compound '$\text{X}$' is:
solution: $\text{SO}_2$ reduces orange acidified potassium dichromate ($\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$) to green chromium(III) sulphate: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + 3\text{SO}_2 \longrightarrow \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{Cr}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3\text{ (green)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

The correct statements among the following are:
(A) Basic vanadium oxide is used in the manufacture of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.
(B) The spin-only magnetic moment value of the transition metal halide employed in Ziegler-Natta polymerization is $2.84\text{ BM}$.
(C) The $p$-block metal compound employed in Ziegler-Natta polymerization has the metal in $+3$ oxidation state.
(D) The number of electrons present in the outermost '$d$' orbital of metal halide employed in Wacker process is $8$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

The correct order of first ($\Delta_i H_1$) and second ($\Delta_i H_2$) ionisation enthalpy values of $\text{Cr}$ and $\text{Mn}$ are:
(A) $\Delta_i H_1 : \text{Cr} > \text{Mn}$
(B) $\Delta_i H_2 : \text{Cr} > \text{Mn}$
(C) $\Delta_i H_1 : \text{Mn} > \text{Cr}$
(D) $\Delta_i H_2 : \text{Mn} > \text{Cr}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution:
For $\Delta_i H_1$: $\text{Mn}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^5 4s^2$, $717\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) $> \text{Cr}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^5 4s^1$, $653\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) (C is correct).
For $\Delta_i H_2$: removing an electron from half-filled $\text{Cr}^+$ ($3d^5$, $1592\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) requires more energy than from $\text{Mn}^+$ ($3d^5 4s^1$, $1509\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$), so $\Delta_i H_2 : \text{Cr} > \text{Mn}$ (B is correct).
Thus, B and C only.

question_text:
Given below are two statements for catalytic properties of transition metals:
Statement I: First row transition metals which act as catalyst utilise their $3d$ electrons only for formation of bonds between reactant molecules and atoms on the surface of catalyst.
Statement II: There is increase in the concentration of reactants on the surface of catalyst which strengthens the bonds in reacting molecules.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution: Statement I is incorrect because transition metals utilise both $3d$ and $4s$ electrons to form bonds with reactant molecules on the catalyst surface. Statement II is incorrect because adsorption increases reactant concentration on the surface and weakens the internal bonds of reacting molecules, thereby lowering the activation energy.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The number of pairs among $[\text{Ti}^{4+}, \text{V}^{2+}]$, $[\text{V}^{2+}, \text{Mn}^{2+}]$, $[\text{Mn}^{2+}, \text{Fe}^{3+}]$ and $[\text{V}^{2+}, \text{Cr}^{2+}]$ in which both ions are coloured is $3$.
Statement II: The number of pairs among $[\text{La}^{3+}, \text{Yb}^{2+}]$, $[\text{Lu}^{3+}, \text{Ce}^{4+}]$ and $[\text{Ac}^{3+}, \text{Lr}^{3+}]$ ions in which both are diamagnetic is $3$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution:
Statement I: $\text{Ti}^{4+}$ ($3d^0$) is colourless, whereas $\text{V}^{2+}$ ($3d^3$), $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($3d^5$), $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($3d^5$), and $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($3d^4$) are coloured. Thus, the $3$ pairs $[\text{V}^{2+}, \text{Mn}^{2+}]$, $[\text{Mn}^{2+}, \text{Fe}^{3+}]$, and $[\text{V}^{2+}, \text{Cr}^{2+}]$ have both ions coloured (True).
Statement II: $\text{La}^{3+}$ ($4f^0$), $\text{Yb}^{2+}$ ($4f^{14}$), $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ ($4f^{14}$), $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ ($4f^0$), $\text{Ac}^{3+}$ ($5f^0$), and $\text{Lr}^{3+}$ ($5f^{14}$) all have $f^0$ or $f^{14}$ configurations with zero unpaired electrons, so all $3$ pairs are diamagnetic (True).
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
